name: A1-02 HTTP Request - pagination, both modes

meta.description: The two pagination modes the HTTP Request node supports, each against a real public API that needs no key, each with a page cap so a misconfigured completion condition cannot loop forever.
meta.author: Suyash Raj - https://rajsuyash.com/blog/n8n-http-request-node-tutorial.html
meta.setup: None. Both APIs are public and unauthenticated.
meta.expectedOutput: 'Offset pagination' returns 150 products from dummyjson.com (3 requests of 50). 'Next-URL pagination' returns 60 Pokemon from pokeapi.co (3 requests of 20). The Code node prints the item count and the number of requests each made.
meta.failureCases: Delete the completeExpression on either node and the node paginates until maxRequests stops it - which is why maxRequests is set. Set limitPagesFetched to false with a wrong completion condition and the node will keep requesting until the workflow times out.

nodes.name: Offset pagination
nodes.notes: $pageCount is 0 on the first request, so skip is 0, 50, 100. The completion condition reads the CURRENT response, not the next one: it stops when a page comes back empty. requestInterval spaces the calls so a burst of pages does not trip a rate limit.

nodes.name: Next-URL pagination
nodes.notes: Use this when the API hands you the next page's URL. nextURL and completeExpression must read the same field, or the node will follow a URL it has already decided is absent.
